messages:
ben: FYI spike during yesterday's canary. host CPU p50 for ingress tokenization climbed ~20% after new kernel scoring landed. profiler points at parse/tokenize/emit smallwrite chain.

ben: sample line: `parse_ms=1.1 tok_ms=0.95 smallwrites=290 kernel_score=stitch_v4 hint=batch_prefer`.

alice: :grimacing: was stitch_v4 the one with the aggressive coalescer? iirc it merges prefixes to maximize GPU batch occupancy.

kevin: yes. stitch_v4 changed the sampler to favor coalescing even for small seqs when it predicts a downstream batch. That can force an extra framing pass on host.

carmen: quick data dump from kvcache: evictions up, hot key churn increased, hitrate fell 0.86 -> 0.75. suspect coalescing creates transient prefix variants.

sanjay: uploaded a flame (small excerpt):
```
1200ms total
  480ms ingress::parse_frame
  420ms tokenizer::tokenize_fastpath
  180ms socket::writev_small
  120ms kvcache::evict_sample
```

ben: tokenizer time being that large is weird; we didn't ship tokenizer changes. hypothesis: extra copy / double-parse when coalesce is enabled.

alice: mitigation options: 1) toggle off coalesce for <64 seq in sampler; 2) include a host_cpu_penalty in kernel scoring; 3) short-term rollback on canary.

kevin: i prototyped adding host_cost est to the kernel profile. new scoring: score = gpu_ms * alpha + host_cost_ms * gamma + mem_penalty * beta. with gamma=0.6 it avoided pick of coalesce kernel for small chatty traces in the sim harness.

carmen: nice. also propose a kvcache dedupe for near-identical prefixes during the coalesce window to reduce eviction noise.

sanjay: can we reproduce locally? i built a harness that replays 10k short requests (avg seq=26) and toggles coalesce. results: p50 host_cpu 18% worse with coalesce on. kv hit down 9%. attached script gist.

ben: decision: roll back on canary to stop customer exposure. then we iterate on sampler score and add small-chat unit test.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary rollout stitch_v4 completed at 2025-05-14T09:03:02Z on cluster-r11.

ben: i'm hitting rollback now.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: rollback stitch_v4 completed at 2025-05-14T09:05:10Z on cluster-r11 12s.

kevin: after rollback p50 host_cpu returned to baseline; kv hit back to ~0.85. i'll open a PR adding host_cost telemetry and a sampler rule: if est_host_penalty > 0.12 and seq_len_median < 60 then prefer legacy kernel.

alice: i'll own bisecting the stitch diff to find whether it's the batching heuristic or the coalesce framing that causes the extra parse. will try isolating the coalesce toggle next.

carmen: i'll add a kvcache probe to log prefix variants and eviction causality. if coalesce causes N variants per request, we can implement a short dedupe window.

sanjay: test plan: add e2e job that runs small-chat replay against candidate kernels and fails if host p50 regresses >10% or kv hit drops >5%.

ben: assign owners: kevin=sampler scoring PR, alice=bisect, carmen=kvcache probe + dedupe RFC, sanjay=harness + e2e job, ben=perf docs + traces.

kevin: one more thought: sampler should sample host telemetry periodically rather than rely solely on offline profiler numbers. add a rolling 5m host_parse_ms metric per kernel tag.

alice: agreed. that will let the scoring adapt to real traffic shapes.

ben: ok closing thread when PRs land. thanks all.
